clue.text: Producing tennis shot — ace

definitions.meaning: hitting an overhead smash, the hard downward stroke in tennis
informal praise meaning excellent or terrific

explanation.surface: A commentator calls a winning tennis shot an ace.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the verb form of hitting a smash, and the British slang adjective for something excellent.

clue.text: County's tail taking lead, recovery finally in the air

indicators.note: the last letter is moved to become the first

parts.note: Hants is the short form of Hampshire, an English county

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An English county's recovery is finally in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. Hants is the usual abbreviation for Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or song, and a shanty is a sailors' work song.

clue.text: Wake refreshed at the farm

indicators.note: refreshed suggests something made over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wakes up feeling restored on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean the consequences following an event, as in the wake of a disaster.

clue.text: Fuel he'd spilled makes one wary

indicators.note: spilled suggests the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man who spilled petrol becomes careful.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedful means paying attention to danger, so it is close to being cautious.

clue.text: Strained marshal clutching bible

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the marshal's name wraps round the bible

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A tense military officer grips a holy book.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervy means tense and jittery, so strained in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Crawling, so getting close

parts.note: so and as both mean in the same way or because
in the hide-and-seek game, warm means getting close to the target

explanation.surface: Something creeps nearer and nearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawling in the sense of teeming or swarming with insects, as in a place crawling with ants.

clue.text: Son's brief insult added spice

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an affront is an insult

explanation.surface: A son's curt rude remark spiced things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a costly yellow spice made from crocus stigmas.

clue.text: A GP touring hospital for a purpose

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the doctor surrounds the hospital letter

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doc
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A family doctor visits a hospital for a particular reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means formed for one particular purpose only.

clue.text: Put on ice dance after second Thursday

indicators.note: after tells us the dance comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An ice dance is staged after a second Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball a plan is to shelve it for later, which is what putting on ice means.

clue.text: Key feature of Restaurant at the End of the Universe?

definitions.text: Key feature of Restaurant at the End of the Universe?

parts.words: Key feature of Restaurant at the End of the Universe?
parts.note: Douglas Adams's restaurant at the end of the universe would have a drinks counter out in the cosmos, and a keyboard has a long key with the same name

explanation.surface: A fan asks what is the main attraction of the restaurant in the Douglas Adams novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bar key on a keyboard, punned as a drinks bar out in space.

clue.text: Proof that a death, sadly, can be sudden

definitions.note: the clue's adjective stands loosely for an adverbial phrase meaning instantly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Evidence that someone can die without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is a link: an action done at the drop of a hat is a sudden one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly and without hesitation, so it describes something done suddenly.

clue.text: Sparing disagreement when it's your round

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the old word for your encircles the quarrel

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
a rift is a split or falling out

explanation.surface: A stingy drinker argues when it is their turn to buy drinks in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your round' plays on a round of drinks bought for a group, a British pub custom; here 'round' just means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrifty means careful with money, which is to be sparing in spending.

clue.text: Middle of ear has painful growth, firm and black

parts.note: a corn is a painful hard growth on the foot
CO is short for company, a firm
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone with an ear infection also has a hard dark lump.
explanation.walkthrough: The ear is an ear of maize, not the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is the central woody core of an ear of maize, carrying the kernels.

clue.text: Arrest a high price to pay for weapon

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to catch or arrest them
in British slang something that costs a bomb is very expensive

explanation.surface: Getting arrested is a heavy cost to bear for carrying arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail bomb is an explosive device packed with nails, an improvised weapon.

clue.text: No longer keen on film sequel?

parts.note: to go off something is to stop liking it
to shoot is to film

explanation.surface: Someone has lost interest in a follow-up movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is something that develops from an original, as a sequel grows from the first story.

clue.text: Irishman, a trainee chauffeur in love

indicators.note: in tells us the article and the learner sit inside the word for zero

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, hence nil
L is a learner driver, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: An Irish chap who is learning to drive has fallen for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Niall is a common Irish man's first name, so an example of an Irishman.

clue.text: During reign some linger on, naturally reflective

indicators.note: reflective suggests a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Throughout a monarch's rule a few people stay on, thinking things over.
explanation.walkthrough: The run INGERONNA sits in 'linger on, naturally' and 'reflective' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in the year of the reign, used in dating statutes.

clue.text: End up swallowing girl's laxative

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the reversed word holds the name
in a down clue, up means reading bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl ends up taking a laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk of magnesia is a familiar laxative and antacid.

clue.text: Old man coming from the east screened for bug

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man
hid means concealed or screened

explanation.surface: A father arriving from the east hides from an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking insect, and bug is a common word for any insect.

clue.text: Type of cup imprisoning genie, bent and stooped

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so the cup size surrounds the rest

parts.note: DD is a bra cup size

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A genie is trapped in a cup and bent over.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, and stooped in the sense of lowering oneself to do something.

clue.text: Fine old boy, I decided

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencil grades
Reg is a boy's name
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A nice old fellow announces his decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A foregone conclusion is one already decided before the event.

clue.text: Adult class bringing in wine regularly

indicators.note: bringing in means taking the letters inside the word for class

parts.note: a group is a class or set

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A grown-up evening class serves wine regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is an adult, as opposed to a child.

clue.text: The people going for promotion

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion
the mass is the people in general

explanation.surface: The public fall for advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Admass is the section of the public easily swayed by advertising and mass media.

clue.text: See presumably only poor wife being locked away

indicators.note: the wife is shut up inside the phrase for not wealthy

parts.note: no rich people, as a joking reading of only poor ones

explanation.surface: A bishop's see seems to contain only paupers and an imprisoned wife.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Norwich is an English cathedral city with its own bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and the Diocese of Norwich is one in eastern England.

clue.text: No ordinary graduate dance

parts.note: rum means odd or strange, no ordinary thing
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: An extraordinary graduate dances.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Threw soldiers into swamp

indicators.note: into means the soldiers are placed inside the word for swamp

parts.note: to flood is to swamp or inundate
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops were dumped in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert them, and floored means utterly baffled.

clue.text: If climbing put on sound footwear and shawl

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards
sound means the letters are what the word is heard as

parts.note: a shoe is footwear, and the French-looking CHU is heard the same way

explanation.surface: Someone climbing puts on sturdy boots and a wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular shawl worn round the neck and shoulders.

clue.text: Opera composed by 1712

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the clue numbers 17 and 12 stand for their answers, the laxative and the maize core

explanation.surface: An opera dated to a year in the early eighteenth century.
explanation.walkthrough: 1712 is not a date: it is clue 17 and clue 12 run together, whose answers MAGNESIA and CORNCOB are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Boccanegra is an opera by Verdi about a Genoese doge.

clue.text: Girl managed to conceal age in answers

indicators.note: in places the shortened word between the two answers

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer, so two As

indicators.note: concealing the age means making those letters vanish from the word

explanation.surface: A girl hid her age in her replies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal age' removes AGE from MANAGED, leaving MAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a girl's name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Examples of squash shoes for gym keep being related

indicators.note: keep means hold inside, so the plimsolls contain the family word

parts.note: pumps are plimsolls, light gym shoes in Britain
kin are relatives, people related to you

explanation.surface: Gym shoes worn while playing squash belong to relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany pumpkins are a kind of squash, the gourd vegetables.
